findings.reason: the author must either extend the existing pace owner or state the cycle that forbids it (hosting `group_pace` in `crew/pace.py` would import `reckon.budget` from a module `budget.py` imports at module level), and that sentence decides the new module's path and name.
findings.text: the plan names the new module `reckon/budget_pace.py` and cites only `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py` as its search result, but `reckon/crew/pace.py` already owns this domain (`policy`, `GroupReading`, `Allowance`, `allowance_for_group`, `allowances_for_groups`; 2,190 tokens) and is imported by the very file being split at `reckon/budget.py:63` (`from reckon.crew import pace as pace_module`), while `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py` owns the lift lifecycle (`end_cause`, `sweep`, `_default_readings`) that the moved `_lift_history`/`_other_session_lift` helpers read — a plan adding a pace module without naming the existing pace owner is exactly the reuse gap this item exists to catch

findings.reason: the bound must be re-based on the post-§46 tree (either raise 45,000 above 46,564, or widen the cut family to include the burn block that pushed it over), otherwise the first implementation node is unachievable as written.
findings.text: the done-when's "at most 45,000 tokens" cannot be met from the base the plan sequences itself behind: §2 dispatches after §46, §46's merge `76946f9a9` is an ancestor of HEAD, and §46's burn block grew `budget.py` from 180,363 to 197,708 bytes (51,533 → 56,488 tokens, +4,955); removing the measured 9,924-token family leaves ~46,564 tokens, so the node fails its own done-when on arrival and the §47 arithmetic ("leaves `budget.py` near 41,600 tokens, which leaves room for §48") is computed at the pre-§46 base

findings.reason: naming the relationship is what stops a later change to `reckon/crew/pace.py` landing without the report, and it is the difference between a module named by what it adds (`pace_report`) and one that reads as a rival owner.
findings.text: `reckon/budget_pace.py` becomes a second module in the tree whose name asserts ownership of pace beside `reckon/crew/pace.py`, with no sentence in the section saying which of the two owns a new pace figure or how a reader is to choose between them; the existing owner is `reckon/crew/pace.py` (paces the week's allowance), and the moved family is the report and hold composed over it, so the two are related but not interchangeable

findings.reason: the re-export is justified by the 16 test files that call through `reckon.budget`, and the plan already repoints any test whose patch stops biting, so this is a sentence to add in the node's brief, not a design change.
findings.text: the plan keeps every moved public name importable from `reckon.budget`, a second name for the same functions; it is justified by real cost (16 test files read them as `budget.<name>`, and 4 of those — `tests/test_picker.py:77`, `tests/test_picker_lanes.py:288`, `tests/test_picker_latency.py:67`, `tests/test_picker_reserved_lanes.py:170` — patch `snapshot.budget.group_pace` to steer `budget.preflight`), but the plan does not state the caveat the layer creates: after the move, intra-module calls inside `budget_pace` resolve in the new module's namespace, so a patch installed on `reckon.budget` no longer reaches the moved functions' calls to each other (e.g. `pace_row`'s call to `group_pace`, `reckon/budget.py:4005`)
